news.headline: Fresh rules issued for dredging in forest areas to mitigate floods
news.story_lead: Fresh rules issued for dredging in forest areas to mitigate floods The Centre has issued fresh guidelines allowing scientifically planned river dredging in forest areas to mitigate floods and restore river ecosystems, without treating the activity as a “non-forest purpose” and exempting qualifying works from forest clearance requirements, compensatory afforestation and net present value (NPV) payments The Centre has issued fresh guidelines allowing scientifically planned river dredging in forest areas to mitigate floods and restore river ecosystems, without treating the activity as a “non-forest purpose” and exempting qualifying works from forest clearance requirements, compensatory afforestation and net present value (NPV) payments. The guidelines come following Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu’s meeting with Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav in September,
news.full_article_text: Fresh rules issued for dredging in forest areas to mitigate floods The Centre has issued fresh guidelines allowing scientifically planned river dredging in forest areas to mitigate floods and restore river ecosystems, without treating the activity as a “non-forest purpose” and exempting qualifying works from forest clearance requirements, compensatory afforestation and net present value (NPV) payments The Centre has issued fresh guidelines allowing scientifically planned river dredging in forest areas to mitigate floods and restore river ecosystems, without treating the activity as a “non-forest purpose” and exempting qualifying works from forest clearance requirements, compensatory afforestation and net present value (NPV) payments. The guidelines come following Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu’s meeting with Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav in September, where he sought a separate framework for dredging in flood-affected rivers. Sukhu had cited the accumulation of debris, silt, stones and boulders after extreme rainfall and flash floods, which narrows river channels and reduces their water-carrying capacity. The guidelines, dated October 27, clarify that scientific, planned and time-bound dredging to remove material accumulated due to natural disasters or extreme weather, restore river flow and protect forest ecosystems would not be treated as a non-forest purpose, provided the prescribed conditions are met. However, the ministry has set conditions to prevent the provision from being used to facilitate commercial extraction. A scientific assessment of the accumulated material by a national institute of repute is mandatory, and a dredging plan must specify the disaster-related justification, quantity of material, methodology, duration, disposal or utilisation and monitoring arrangements. “The Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Head of Forest Force of the concerned state shall furnish a certificate specifying that the dredging is necessary to restore the natural course and flow of the river due to the natural disaster, and that the activity contributes to the restoration, protection and management of forest and riverine ecosystems,” said the guidelines, which HT has seen. Further, the dredging plan must be recommended by the district disaster management authority, chaired by the district collector, and approved by the state disaster management authority, chaired by the chief secretary. The activity must also be incorporated into the forest division’s working plan, with proposals processed through the ministry’s PARIVESH portal. “The dredged material originating from forest lands shall be treated as forest produce. The removal, handling, transportation and disposal of the dredged material shall be carried out in accordance with the applicable state forest laws, rules and codal provisions,” it adds, specifying these guidelines will not apply to activities undertaken primarily for commercial extraction of minerals or riverbed material, or where royalty is levied on the disposal of dredged material. Experts however said the focus should be on conservation and prevention of any disasters or floods — beginning with efforts to prevent buildings coming up along river catchments or in sensitive hilly areas. “Such initiatives can be thought of when all conservation and preventive measure has been taken and not as the sole solution. At the same time, we will have to look at the grey area possibly where agencies may argue any activity being undertaken near the river is for protection of the river, even if it is not,” said Prakriti Srivastava, a retired IFS officer, who has served as the deputy inspector general of forests (wildlife) in the environment ministry. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jasjeev Gandhiok Jasjeev Gandhiok is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times, where he covers environment, climate change, the clean energy transition and wildlife at the National Bureau. Gandhiok has over a decade of experience in journalism and is based in Delhi. He has reported extensively on Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR). This includes the region's air pollution woes, a polluted Yamuna and on urban wildlife still thriving in the region. He joined HT in October 2021. Prior to that, he had five-year stint at The Times of India in Delhi, where he also covered Delhi, with a focus on environment and wildlife. Gandhiok has covered some recent events around the Capital too, ranging from the farmers' protests, the northeast Delhi riots and the CAA-NRC protests, reporting from the ground on all of these. He also travels across the country to report on how environment and climate change impact everyday life, while also writing on endangered species. His reports in 2019 on toxic leachate from Delhi's landfills led to the National Green Tribunal (NGT) taking suo motu cognisance and ultimately asking the state government to start bio-mining to flatten and remove all three landfills in the capital. He also closely tracks the implementation of government policies on climate, renewable energy and environmental protection. His focus remains on impactful, public-interest journalism which explains how environmental decisions affect people's everyday lives. Read More

news.headline: Nicobarese tribal leaders ‘not necessary or proper parties’ in Great Nicobar forest rights case: Centre tells Calcutta HC
news.story_lead: Nicobarese tribal leaders ‘not necessary or proper parties’ in Great Nicobar forest rights case: Centre tells Calcutta HC The dispute concerns the validity of the process through which forest rights were recognised, paving the way for Centre’s ₹ 81,000-crore Great Nicobar project. The Centre has opposed a plea by four Nicobarese tribal representatives to join a case challenging the recognition of forest rights on Great Nicobar Island, telling the Calcutta high court that they are not "necessary or proper parties" and have approached the court after an unexplained delay. The Centre has opposed a plea by four Nicobarese tribal representatives to join a case challenging the recognition of forest rights on Great Nicobar Island, telling the Calcutta high court that they are not "necessary or proper parties" and have approached the court after an unexplained delay. The dispute concerns the validity of the process through which forest rights were recognised in 2022, paving the way for the Centre’s ₹ 81,000-crore Great Nicobar Island development project. “The applicants bypassed statutory remedies under FRA (Forest Rights Act) and cannot seek party status after a gross delay (nearly four years from the certificate and two years after the writ petition,” the Ministry of tribal affairs has said in an affidavit seen by HT. The four applicants -- Barnabas Manju, Titus, Hosie and Hopeful-- belong to the Nicobarese community and had sought to be impleaded as respondents in a public interest litigation filed by former IAS officer Meena Gupta. The petition challenges the constitution of the Sub-Divisional Level Committee (SDLC) under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006, the proceedings recorded as Gram Sabha resolutions, and the forest rights recognition certificate issued on August 18, 2022. The FRA provides for the recognition of individual and community forest rights through a process involving Gram Sabhas and committees at the sub-divisional and district levels. The ongoing case questions whether the statutory process was followed before forest land was diverted for the project. While Manju is the chairperson of the Tribal Council of Little Nicobar and Great Nicobar, Campbell Bay, Titus is a native of Pulo Bhabi village on the west coast of Great Nicobar and was elected as the first village captain of Pulo Bhabi in 2018. Hosie has served as the second village captain of Pulo Bhabi village since 2018, while Hopeful is a native of Kokeon village in Great Nicobar and sought after within the community for his knowledge of medicinal herbs, plant parts used for repair of traditional huts, hunting and fishing techniques, as well as boating and navigation skills. Centre's arguments In its affidavit, the Ministry has argued that the applicants had not raised objections through the statutory mechanisms provided under the law. “Answering respondent states and humbly submits on the preliminary submissions that the application is barred by delay and laches. No objections were raised through statutory channels under FRA during the relevant period. The applicants’ own annexures substantiate that no formal objections were received from the Tribal Council at the material time.” “The applicants are not necessary or proper parties,” it adds. The Centre, in its response, has also maintained that the Nicobarese community’s interests were adequately represented by the official respondents and that the tribal council had representation on the SDLC. It disputed allegations of procedural irregularities, stating that Gram Sabhas in Campbell Bay, Laxmi Nagar and Govind Nagar were convened on August 12, 2022, and that the forest rights certificate was issued after due process. What the tribal representatives say The tribal representatives, however, have alleged that the process did not secure the consent of the Nicobarese community. Their application states that no Gram Sabha of the Nicobarese was convened under the FRA to discuss the diversion of their ancestral forest land. It also alleges that Manju, chairperson of the Tribal Council of Little and Great Nicobar, was not informed that he was a member of the SDLC until he attended its meeting on August 13, 2022. Manju subsequently withdrew his no-objection certificate through a letter dated November 22, 2022, claiming that he had not been given adequate information to make an informed decision. The Calcutta high court has scheduled the next hearing for November 25 and 26. The dispute has significant implications for the proposed development project, which includes a transhipment port, a greenfield international airport, a township, and power infrastructure across 166 sq km of the island. The Nicobarese community has also sought to return to ancestral villages after being displaced by the 2004 tsunami. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jasjeev Gandhiok Jasjeev Gandhiok is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times, where he covers environment, climate change, the clean energy transition and wildlife at the National Bureau. He also travels across the country to report on how environment and climate change impact everyday life, while also writing on endangered species. The development comes a day after a major daylight robbery took place in Chandni Chowk on Wednesday morning where four armed men entered an office, robbed ₹ 2.3 crore cash and fled. news.full_article_text: Chandni Chowk robbery: Traders complain of minimal police deployment in market area Delhi Police said sufficient staff is deployed in the market but due to extreme narrow lanes, it becomes tough to control crowds and prevent such robberies Traders in Chandni Chowk have expressed their dismay in the lack of proper police deployment that has led to encroachment, robberies and lawlessness in the area. The development comes a day after a major daylight robbery took place in Chandni Chowk on Wednesday morning where four armed men entered an office, robbed ₹ 2.3 crore cash and fled. Sanjay Bhargava, a businessman and president of the Sarv Vyapar Mandal in Chandni Chowk, said, “There’s not one issue here. There are multiple. Everyday, we see hundreds of drug addicts, ruffians, pickpockets and thieves. But not a single policeman is seen in the market. There’s also heavy encroachment but the police do nothing. By law, no vehicles are allowed inside the market but everyone gets their mini trucks and bikes. It’s a completely lawless area”, he said. Also Read: In and out with ₹ 2.3 crore: Robbers strike office in Chandni Chowk “We all know most of the robberies are because outsiders or an employee (insider) is doing some sort of spying and colluding with criminal gangs. But why is it that the police can never catch them? There are police posts but the staff hardly leaves the post area. Home guards are deployed sometimes but they don’t even understand the market because they are not from Delhi. Police have no control over pickpockets, ruffians or criminal gangs working here. It’s peak festival season but deployment is so so low”, he added. Meanwhile, the Delhi Police said sufficient staff is deployed in the market but due to extreme narrow lanes and crowded spaces, it becomes tough to control crowds and prevent such robberies. "We have deployed local staff along with more than 120 home guards. The staff does regular patrolling as well. However, one can't identify an informer or someone who's just roaming around and doing recce in a crowded market. We also have to look at crowd control, traffic issues along with law and order. We try and do patrolling at least thrice a day. Since vehicles can't go inside market, we do bike patrolling and on foot patrolling", a senior police officer in northern range said. Also Read: BJP holds ‘Save democracy’ rally in Delhi’s Chandni Chowk Yogesh Singhal, chairman of the Bullion and Jewellers Association in Kucha Mahajani, said traders were increasingly worried about their safety. “We are all living in fear as this keeps happening at our shops as well as offices nearby. Businessmen and their employees are also targeted on bikes or in cars near Chandni Chowk. They are followed and then robbed. There are major security issues here. There’s hardly any deployment here,” he said, adding that the gang on Wednesday appeared to have chosen the morning as the market was not yet crowded. “We keep telling local staff to increase deployment but not much is done,” he said. Also Read: Delhi govt, MCD sign MoU for Chandni Chowk town hall redevelopment Chandni Chowk trader and Bharatiya Vyapar Mandal Udyog member Jagmohan Gotewale also echoed similar sentiments over the lack of police personnel. “A lot of cash transactions take place in Chandni Chowk, and somewhere or the other, staff or other people leak information, which leads to such major crimes. The biggest requirement in Chandni Chowk is an increase in police patrolling. Along with that, local traders are already suffering because our business has been stifled by online shopping and restrictions in Chandni Chowk, such as cars not being allowed to run, scooters not coming in, and an excessive number of rickshaws, which has already reduced business. On top of that, after such incidents occur, people who come to buy items with cash avoid coming to Chandni Chowk out of fear that some mishap might happen to them”, Gotewale said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jignasa Sinha Jignasa Sinha is a Special Correspondent at Hindustan Times in New Delhi. With more than six years of reporting experience, she covers crime and policing in the national capital. Her beats also include Delhi prisons, the Delhi Fire Services and Delhi courts, while she regularly reports on gender, labour and social justice. Over the course of her career, Jignasa has reported on major criminal investigations, international crime syndicates, high-profile cyber fraud cases, law-and-order developments, protests, disasters and public institutions. Her reporting combines breaking news with in-depth, long form, human interest stories that examine the human impact of public policy, policing and the criminal justice system. In addition to reporting for the newspaper, she contributes to the Hindustan Times website and app, and plays an active role in coordinating on-ground coverage of major developments and breaking news across Delhi. Before joining Hindustan Times, Jignasa worked at The Indian Express newspaper in New Delhi, where she spent five years covering crime, Delhi airport, courts and health. She began her journalism career as an intern at an AI magazine in Bengaluru while pursuing her postgraduate diploma in multimedia journalism at the Indian Institute of Journalism and New Media. news.headline: ‘Not opposed, making heartfelt plea’: Delhi traders urge Sonia Gandhi to postpone November 1 Ramlila Maidan rally
news.story_lead: ‘Not opposed, making heartfelt plea’: Delhi traders urge Sonia Gandhi to postpone November 1 Ramlila Maidan rally Citing severe economic fallout during the peak festive period, the premier traders' body warned of a severe traffic paralysis across 20 historic markets. The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) on Thursday wrote directly to Congress Parliamentary Party Chairperson Sonia Gandhi , demanding an immediate deferral of the INDIA bloc’s massive November 1 mega-rally at Ramlila Maidan . Citing severe economic fallout during the peak festive shopping period, the premier traders' body warned that bringing an estimated 10 lakh (1 million) people and 15,000 to 20,000 vehicles into Central Delhi would spark a severe traffic paralysis across 20 historic markets.
news.full_article_text: ‘Not opposed, making heartfelt plea’: Delhi traders urge Sonia Gandhi to postpone November 1 Ramlila Maidan rally Citing severe economic fallout during the peak festive period, the premier traders' body warned of a severe traffic paralysis across 20 historic markets. The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) on Thursday wrote directly to Congress Parliamentary Party Chairperson Sonia Gandhi , demanding an immediate deferral of the INDIA bloc’s massive November 1 mega-rally at Ramlila Maidan . Citing severe economic fallout during the peak festive shopping period, the premier traders' body warned that bringing an estimated 10 lakh (1 million) people and 15,000 to 20,000 vehicles into Central Delhi would spark a severe traffic paralysis across 20 historic markets. "We demand to reschedule the mega-rally of 1 million (10 lakh) people, planned for November 1, to a date after Diwali; lack of parking for 15,000–20,000 vehicles could lead to a total gridlock, akin to a lockdown," the CTI urged in its letter to Sonia Gandhi. ‘Not opposed to rally, making heartfelt plea’ Deep Dive The planned rally comes at a critical juncture for Delhi's commercial ecosystem. With Dhanteras falling on November 6 and Diwali on November 8, traders emphasise that November 1 represents the busiest single day for festive inventory transit and shopper movement. CTI Chairman Brijesh Goyal stressed that business owners are facing widespread panic, clarifying that their plea is purely about survival rather than political opposition. "We are not opposing the rally; we are making a heartfelt plea to protect our livelihoods during the peak Diwali season," stated CTI Chairman Brijesh Goyal. "These 20 markets are not merely marketplaces; they are the heartbeat of Delhi. They generate a daily turnover of 10,000 to 12,000 crore rupees, and Dhanteras falls on November 6th. Traders are anxious: if a lockdown-like gridlock hits central Delhi on October 31st and November 1st, how will the goods for Dhanteras be transported in and out?" Goyal added. "Dhanteras falls on November 6, and Diwali is on November 8; November 1 is the busiest day for preparations... If 1 million people and 15,000–20,000 vehicles arrive in Central Delhi on November 1, the daily business turnover of ₹ 10,000–12,000 crore across 20 historic markets will come to a complete standstill," Goyal noted. Transporters refuse to dispatch stock amid deadlock concerns In its representation, the CTI detailed four major points of concern that could cripple capital logistics starting as early as Thursday evening: Lack of parking at Ramlila Maidan. "Where will 15,000–20,000 vehicles be parked? Ramlila Maidan does not even have the capacity to park 200 large buses." They also raised concern over the threat to 20 historic wholesale & retail hubs. "20 historic wholesale and retail markets within a 5 km radius, with a daily turnover of ₹ 10,000–12,000 crore." Several historic markets within a 5 km radius have been affected, including Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazar, Connaught Place, Palika Bazar, Janpath, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Kashmiri Gate, Naya Bazar, Lajpat Rai Market, Chawri Bazar, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Ballimaran, Fatehpuri, Tilak Bazar, Karol Bagh, Jama Masjid, Nabi Karim, Gaffar Market, Ajmeri Gate-Paharganj and Daryaganj. Also Read I 3,000 cops, heavily barricaded roads as Delhi's Ramlila Maidan fortified ahead of Congress-led rally on November 1 The trade body also raised the issue of premature border & arterial gridlock and previous protests that dented the profits of shopkeepers in the peak festival season. Starting from the afternoon of October 31st, buses and vehicles may begin arriving at Delhi’s borders—Singhu, Tikri, Ghazipur, and Badarpur. By the evening, barricades could be set up along Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg and JLN Marg. Transporters are already refusing to dispatch vehicles from October 31st." "On October 10th, with only 5,000 to 7,000 people gathering at Jantar Mantar , central Delhi remained gridlocked for eight hours. Now, 1 million (10 lakh) people are expected to arrive." The trade body highlighted that these hubs—some up to 300 years old—supply goods pan-India and depend on 5,000 daily trucks and tempos arriving from 56 industrial areas (including Narela, Bawana, Okhla, Mayapuri, Mundka, Udyog Nagar, and Mangolpuri). CTI proposes alternatives for Congress march To prevent a total commercial shutdown, the Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) suggested two alternatives: rescheduling the event to after the peak festive season, preferably beyond November 10, or relocating the rally to Burari Maidan if holding it on November 1 is non-negotiable. Meanwhile, the rally—dubbed the 'Chalo Dilli Ramlila March'—has been called by the opposition INDIA bloc to demonstrate against alleged vote tampering. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi emphasised that the movement transcends individual party lines: "Chalo Dilli Ramlila March, it is a march to save democracy, to stop vote theft, to save the Constitution. This is not a march of any one political party; it is a march of the soul of India. All the people who are fed up with Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, and Gyanesh Kumar, all the people who want to save democracy, who want to protect the Constitution, you all come," Rahul Gandhi stated. With less than 48 hours remaining before the scheduled assembly, traders in the national capital await an official response from Congress leadership regarding their request.

news.full_article_text: This is the first time in Xi's 14 years of leadership that plenum attendance fell below 300 - Published 29 October 2026 A record 33 members have been expelled from China's Communist Party as it concluded a major annual political gathering, which had the most empty seats ever seen. The fifth plenum was attended by 279 Central Committee members, compared to 315 at the fourth plenum in October 2025 and 364 at the third one in July 2024. While recent plenums focused on economic reforms or social and development issues, party discipline took centre stage at this week's gathering. Xi Jinping has made the fight against corruption a central pillar of his rule since he took the reins in 2012, calling it the "biggest threat" to the party. Since then, more than two million individuals have been disciplined for cases related to "pointless formalities, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance", Zhang Fuhai, from the party's disciplinary commission, told a press briefing on Friday. He also said the party would enhance its efforts to ensure officials "dare not, cannot, and do not want to be corrupt". Anti-corruption purges continue Sixteen of the 33 members expelled are from the military, according to a communique issued on Thursday, which marked the end of the four-day closed-door gathering held at a hotel in Beijing. It's unclear what specific charges these members face beyond "serious disciplinary and legal violations". Such broad allegations have become routine under Xi's anti-corruption campaign. It has now become "an effort to consolidate and maintain authority", says Chong Ja Ian, a non-resident scholar with Carnegie China. "In this case, the campaign will continue and expand depending on how secure Xi feels rather than any real issue with corruption." In its statement, the party said it has "squarely confronted the grim reality that party leadership had at times weakened or hollowed out" and that it will continue to "enforce strict party self-governance, including turning the knife inwards to... curb disorder". The latest expulsions bring the total number of members removed under Xi's third term to a record 51, up from 35 and five in his first and second terms respectively. Beyond the plenum, China's top anti-corruption watchdog reported that 680,000 people across the party apparatus have been disciplined in the first nine months of this year. This is also the first time in Xi's 14 years of leadership that plenum attendance fell below 300. The current Central Committee started its term in 2022 with more than 370 members. Observers argue that Xi views corruption not just as graft but also ideological impurity and, crucially, disloyalty. In January, he warned against "two-faced cadres" who profess political loyalty but defy orders and act in their self-interest. The party says it's going after "pointless formalities", which inlcude "bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance" Who are the key figures purged? Among the high-ranking officials expelled are former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui, and ex-top generals Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli. Official statements announcing their removal this year said they "seriously violating [the party's] discipline and rules", which is widely read as a euphemism for corruption. The culling of the military's top brass has been particularly significant, with Neil Thomas, Lobsang Tsering and Shengyu Wang from the Asia Society Policy Institute describing it as "in a category of its own". "It raises serious questions about organisational leadership and combat readiness, even as China continues to unveil formidable new military hardware," they wrote. Zhang was also vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission, which controls the armed forces. The seven-member commission has since been whittled down to just two members: Xi as chairman and Zhang Shengmin vice-chairman. Ma and Zhang Youxia were former Politburo members. Their removal, along with former general He Weidong in 2025, meant the powerful 24-man Politburo was at one point left with 21 members. Zhang Shengmin was promoted to the top decision-making body at the fifth plenum, bringing the number to 22. Former prominent diplomat Liu Jianchao, who disappeared from public view in July last year, was also named among those who have been purged. news.headline: Israel Election Impasse, Bhutan Glacial Lake Outburst Triggers Bengal Alert, and Delhi AQI Improves
news.story_lead: A series of major national and international developments unfolded today, including political deadlock in Israel as no bloc secured a legislative majority, and a glacial lake outburst in Bhutan prompting flood alerts in northern West Bengal. Meanwhile, overnight precipitation in New Delhi led to a notable improvement in air quality, bringing the Air Quality Index down to satisfactory levels.
news.full_article_text:
### Israel Election Results and Political Stalemate
Israel's parliamentary election counting concluded without any political bloc securing the 61-seat threshold required to form a majority government in the 120-member parliament. 
- **Netanyahu Bloc**: Secured 53 seats.
- **Opposition Camp (led by Gadi Eisenkot)**: Won 48 seats.
- **Arab Parties (Joint List and Ra'am)**: Combined total of 19 seats.
- **Political Dynamics**: With neither major coalition reaching 61 seats, attention has shifted to the potential role of Arab political factions in coalition negotiations.

### Bhutan Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF) Alert in West Bengal
Authorities in West Bengal issued an alert for parts of the northern Dooars region following a glacial lake outburst event in neighboring Bhutan.
- **Location**: The outburst took place at the Shintaphu glacial lake, situated beneath Wakila Mountain in Bhutan's Gasa district.
- **Impact Zone**: West Bengal officials are monitoring water levels along the Sankosh River, with specific oversight focused on the Kumargram area in Alipurduar district.

### Meteorological Relief and AQI Drop in Delhi
Overnight rainfall across the National Capital Region delivered temporary relief from atmospheric pollution and lowered ambient temperatures.
- **AQI Movement**: Delhi's Air Quality Index dropped to 90 (Satisfactory) at 9:05 AM, reflecting a 132-point improvement from Thursday's 4:00 PM reading of 222 (Poor).
- **Station Data**: Out of all active monitoring stations, 16 registered air quality in the 'Moderate' range, while all remaining stations recorded 'Satisfactory' levels.

### Notable Developments in Sports and Culture
- **WPL Auction Milestone**: Karnataka all-rounder Uma Kashvi became the youngest player ever selected in Women's Premier League (WPL) auction history. She is currently competing in the Women's U-19 T20 Challenger Trophy in Bilaspur.
- **Obituary**: Renowned actor Sir Patrick Stewart, celebrated for his iconic roles in 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men', passed away in Los Angeles at the age of 86 due to complications from Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.

hindi_translation.headline: इजराइल चुनावों में गतिरोध, भूटान में ग्लेशियर झील फटने से पश्चिम बंगाल में अलर्ट, दिल्ली की वायु गुणवत्ता में सुधार
hindi_translation.story_lead: आज कई प्रमुख राष्ट्रीय और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय घटनाक्रम सामने आए। इजराइल में किसी भी राजनीतिक गुट को बहुमत न मिलने से राजनीतिक गतिरोध उत्पन्न हो गया है, जबकि भूटान में ग्लेशियर झील फटने के बाद उत्तरी पश्चिम बंगाल में बाढ़ का अलर्ट जारी किया गया है। इस बीच, दिल्ली में रातभर हुई बारिश से वायु गुणवत्ता सूचकांक में बड़ा सुधार दर्ज किया गया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### इजराइल चुनाव परिणाम और राजनीतिक गतिरोध
इजराइल के संसदीय चुनावों की मतगणना पूरी हो चुकी है, जिसमें किसी भी राजनीतिक समूह को 120 सदस्यीय संसद में सरकार बनाने के लिए आवश्यक 61 सीटों का स्पष्ट बहुमत नहीं मिला है।
- **नेतान्याहू गुट**: 53 सीटें जीतीं।
- **विपक्षी खेमा (गादी ईसेनकोट के नेतृत्व में)**: 48 सीटें हासिल कीं।
- **अरब पार्टियां (जॉइंट लिस्ट और राअम)**: कुल 19 सीटें प्राप्त कीं।
- **राजनीतिक स्थिति**: 61 सीटों का आंकड़ा न छू पाने के कारण अब सरकार गठन में अरब राजनीतिक दलों की भूमिका महत्वपूर्ण हो गई है।

### भूटान में ग्लेशियर झील का फटना (GLOF) और पश्चिम बंगाल में अलर्ट
भूटान में ग्लेशियर झील फटने की घटना के बाद पश्चिम बंगाल प्रशासन ने उत्तरी डुआर्स क्षेत्र में सतर्कता बढ़ा दी है।
- **स्थान**: यह घटना भूटान के गासा जिले में वाकिला पर्वत के नीचे स्थित शिंताफू ग्लेशियर झील में हुई।
- **प्रभावित क्षेत्र**: पश्चिम बंगाल के अधिकारी संकोश नदी के जलस्तर पर नज़र बनाए हुए हैं, विशेषकर अलीपुरद्वार जिले के कुमारग्राम क्षेत्र में।

### दिल्ली में बारिश से प्रदूषण में राहत
राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र में रातभर हुई बारिश से तापमान में गिरावट आई और प्रदूषण से राहत मिली।
- **AQI में सुधार**: दिल्ली का वायु गुणवत्ता सूचकांक गिरकर 90 (संतोषजनक श्रेणी) पर आ गया, जो बृहस्पतिवार शाम के 222 (खराब श्रेणी) से 132 अंक कम है।
- **स्टेशनों का डेटा**: 16 मॉनिटरिंग स्टेशनों पर AQI मध्यम श्रेणी में रहा, जबकि बाकी स्टेशनों पर यह संतोषजनक दर्ज किया गया।

### खेल और सांस्कृतिक समाचार
- **WPL नीलामी रिकॉर्ड**: कर्नाटक की ऑलराउंडर उमा काश्वी महिला प्रीमियर लीग (WPL) इतिहास में चुनी जाने वाली सबसे कम उम्र की खिलाड़ी बन गईं।
- **निधन**: 'एक्स-मेन' और 'स्टार ट्रेक' फ्रैंचाइज़ी के लिए प्रसिद्ध वरिष्ठ अभिनेता सर पैट्रिक स्टीवर्ट का 86 वर्ष की आयु में लॉस एंजिल्स में निधन हो गया।

अरब पार्टियों 'जॉइंट लिस्ट' और 'राअम' को कुल 19 सीटें मिलीं, जिससे वे निर्णायक स्थिति में आ गई हैं।
भूटान के गासा जिले में स्थित शिंताफू ग्लेशियर झील फटने से पश्चिम बंगाल के निचले इलाकों में अलर्ट जारी किया गया।

दिल्ली का वायु गुणवत्ता सूचकांक (AQI) 222 से घटकर 90 पर पहुंचा, जिससे हवा 'संतोषजनक' श्रेणी में आ गई।
उमा काश्वी WPL इतिहास की सबसे कम उम्र की खिलाड़ी बनीं।

news.full_article_text: Supreme Court rejects Mahua Moitra’s plea on AIF-FPI ownership disclosure The court said that its order will not come in the way of the Centre or the Securities Exchange Board of India (SEBI) from framing a policy as there is presently no legal or regulatory framework mandating public disclosure of beneficial owners of Alternate Investment Fund (AIF) and Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPI) The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a petition filed by Trinamool Congress (TMC) lawmaker Mahua Moitra questioning the opacity of beneficial owners of portfolio funds having a market capitalisation of over ₹ 90 lakh crore. The court said that its order will not come in the way of the Centre or the Securities Exchange Board of India (SEBI) from framing a policy as there is presently no legal or regulatory framework mandating public disclosure of beneficial owners of Alternate Investment Fund (AIF) and Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPI). A bench headed by justice BV Nagarathna said, “We find that in exercise of our powers under Article 32 of the Constitution, such a prayer cannot be granted as the framework for full public disclosure mandates a legal and regulatory framework. In the absence of this, the court cannot mandate such disclosure. In these circumstances, the prayer sought cannot be granted.” The petition was argued by advocate Prashant Bhushan who said that absence of any regulatory or legal framework cannot be a ground for not entertaining the petition. He pointed out that in the past, the court has intervened by directing the Election Commission to mandate disclosure by candidates of their criminal antecedents, educational qualifications, assets and liabilities when there was no legal requirement to do so. The bench, also comprising justices R Mahadevan and DK Upadhyaya said, “That was electoral reforms. It cannot be compared with this case. It is ultimately for the Union of India and SEBI to put a framework in place under which such a public disclosure can be mandated.” Solicitor general Tushar Mehta appearing for Centre and SEBI questioned the maintainability of the petitioner who is a MP. He said, “The purpose of this petition is to stop foreign direct investment. This very issue was examined earlier by this court and a finding was given. Such disclosure will be devastating.” Even the bench asked Bhushan, “We are not on merits but at whose instance we have to consider this matter. She is a member of Parliament. If she wants a discussion on this issue, she has the right to raise it in Parliament. But entertaining a petition under Article 32 has its ramifications.” The court clarified that it has nothing against the petitioner who, while an MP, has approached this court by filing a petition under Article 32 challenging the remission granted to the Bilkis Bano rape convicts that was entertained along with similar pleas by other civil society members. Bhushan said that it will be a “dangerous proposition” to lay down that a MP cannot approach the court under Article 32. He said, “To have a debate in Parliament is not very easy. Being a member of Parliament does not disentitle her as she has approached this court as a citizen who is also a MP. She is raising a matter in public interest as she is concerned about the fate of 14 crore innocent investors who have invested in stocks which are manipulated by such opaque entities.” The bench said, “We are not saying anything in Parliament. But why does she want to lend her name in this matter? None of the investors has come before us.” When Bhushan said she is one of the investors, the bench added, “ That makes it a private interest. A petition under Article 32 is for ordinary persons who cannot access the courts. Such PILs we have always entertained in the past for which we bow down to our predecessors.” Moitra had earlier sent a representation to SEBI that was replied to on September 19, 2025. According to the petition, the two funds (AIF and FPI) hold significant market share with assets under management (AUM) of AIFs showing an increase of over 300% from ₹ 1,437 crore (at the end of FY 2013) to ₹ 13 lakh crore by end of December 2024. Even the asset under custody of registered FPIs is over ₹ 78.6 lakh crore compared to MFs having over ₹ 75 lakh crore as on July 31, 2025. Bhushan pointed out that such funds now account for over ₹ 100 lakh crore which poses risk of money laundering, tax evasion and market manipulation. SEBI in its response dismissed the concerns raised by Moitra pointing out that the beneficial owners of AFIs/FPIs exceeding a 10% threshold in terms of ownership, control, or economic interest are required to be identified under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA) and the Prevention of Money-Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005. “These laws uniformly apply to all reporting entities (as defined in PMLA) including those registered and regulated by SEBI,” the response said. Moitra points out in her petition that despite having SEBI Regulations of 2012 governing AIFs and SEBI Regulations 2019 governing FPIs, there is no disclosure to investors, statement of portfolio, half-yearly or periodic disclosures, or annual reports of these funds disclosed publicly which affects retail investors. SEBI’s reply said, “While investor confidentiality is preserved in line with global standards, SEBI and other enforcement agencies have visibility into the beneficial ownership and portfolio details of both AIFs and FPIs, in line with the requirements under PMLA.” The AIF Regulations and FPI Regulations do not mandate public disclosure of entity-wise investments. However, disclosures of investments by every AIF/FPI are in fact made to SEBI/custodians which enable regulation, detailed investigation when circumstances warrant and support policy formulation,” states SEBI. Moitra’s petition, filed as a public interest litigation (PIL), said that at a time when retail investors in mutual funds (MF) are put to strict scrutiny by SEBI, the retail investors are kept in the dark about beneficiary owners of these two funds. “Lack of public disclosure poses severe risk to financial stability, market integrity, and economic sovereignty…Increasing foreign investment into Indian market and absence of ultimate beneficiary owners disclosure norms raise concern over possible money laundering (round tripping of funds), tax evasion and market manipulation,” Moitra stated in her petition. Given the increasing role of AFIs and FPIs in the Indian financial market, the petition underlined that “regulatory transparency is crucial for protecting the interest of market stakeholders, especially retail investors.” This, in turn, would ensure market stability and prevent financial malpractices by circumventing laws,” she added. As per the petition, SEBI has 1,647 registered AIFs holding assets worth ₹ 14.17 lakh crore and 11,999 FPIs with assets worth ₹ 78.66 lakh crore.

hindi_translation.full_article_text: Supreme Court rejects Mahua Moitra’s plea on AIF-FPI ownership disclosure The court said that its order will not come in the way of the Centre or the Securities Exchange Board of India (SEBI) from framing a policy as there is presently no legal or regulatory framework mandating public disclosure of beneficial owners of Alternate Investment Fund (AIF) and Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPI) The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a petition filed by Trinamool Congress (TMC) lawmaker Mahua Moitra questioning the opacity of beneficial owners of portfolio funds having a market capitalisation of over ₹ 90 lakh crore. The court said that its order will not come in the way of the Centre or the Securities Exchange Board of India (SEBI) from framing a policy as there is presently no legal or regulatory framework mandating public disclosure of beneficial owners of Alternate Investment Fund (AIF) and Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPI). A bench headed by justice BV Nagarathna said, “We find that in exercise of our powers under Article 32 of the Constitution, such a prayer cannot be granted as the framework for full public disclosure mandates a legal and regulatory framework. In the absence of this, the court cannot mandate such disclosure. In these circumstances, the prayer sought cannot be granted.” The petition was argued by advocate Prashant Bhushan who said that absence of any regulatory or legal framework cannot be a ground for not entertaining the petition. He pointed out that in the past, the court has intervened by directing the Election Commission to mandate disclosure by candidates of their criminal antecedents, educational qualifications, assets and liabilities when there was no legal requirement to do so. The bench, also comprising justices R Mahadevan and DK Upadhyaya said, “That was electoral reforms. It cannot be compared with this case. It is ultimately for the Union of India and SEBI to put a framework in place under which such a public disclosure can be mandated.” Solicitor general Tushar Mehta appearing for Centre and SEBI questioned the maintainability of the petitioner who is a MP. He said, “The purpose of this petition is to stop foreign direct investment. This very issue was examined earlier by this court and a finding was given. Such disclosure will be devastating.” Even the bench asked Bhushan, “We are not on merits but at whose instance we have to consider this matter. She is a member of Parliament. If she wants a discussion on this issue, she has the right to raise it in Parliament. But entertaining a petition under Article 32 has its ramifications.” The court clarified that it has nothing against the petitioner who, while an MP, has approached this court by filing a petition under Article 32 challenging the remission granted to the Bilkis Bano rape convicts that was entertained along with similar pleas by other civil society members. Bhushan said that it will be a “dangerous proposition” to lay down that a MP cannot approach the court under Article 32. He said, “To have a debate in Parliament is not very easy. Being a member of Parliament does not disentitle her as she has approached this court as a citizen who is also a MP. She is raising a matter in public interest as she is concerned about the fate of 14 crore innocent investors who have invested in stocks which are manipulated by such opaque entities.” The bench said, “We are not saying anything in Parliament. But why does she want to lend her name in this matter? None of the investors has come before us.” When Bhushan said she is one of the investors, the bench added, “ That makes it a private interest. A petition under Article 32 is for ordinary persons who cannot access the courts. Such PILs we have always entertained in the past for which we bow down to our predecessors.” Moitra had earlier sent a representation to SEBI that was replied to on September 19, 2025. According to the petition, the two funds (AIF and FPI) hold significant market share with assets under management (AUM) of AIFs showing an increase of over 300% from ₹ 1,437 crore (at the end of FY 2013) to ₹ 13 lakh crore by end of December 2024. Even the asset under custody of registered FPIs is over ₹ 78.6 lakh crore compared to MFs having over ₹ 75 lakh crore as on July 31, 2025. Bhushan pointed out that such funds now account for over ₹ 100 lakh crore which poses risk of money laundering, tax evasion and market manipulation. SEBI in its response dismissed the concerns raised by Moitra pointing out that the beneficial owners of AFIs/FPIs exceeding a 10% threshold in terms of ownership, control, or economic interest are required to be identified under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA) and the Prevention of Money-Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005. “These laws uniformly apply to all reporting entities (as defined in PMLA) including those registered and regulated by SEBI,” the response said. Moitra points out in her petition that despite having SEBI Regulations of 2012 governing AIFs and SEBI Regulations 2019 governing FPIs, there is no disclosure to investors, statement of portfolio, half-yearly or periodic disclosures, or annual reports of these funds disclosed publicly which affects retail investors. SEBI’s reply said, “While investor confidentiality is preserved in line with global standards, SEBI and other enforcement agencies have visibility into the beneficial ownership and portfolio details of both AIFs and FPIs, in line with the requirements under PMLA.” The AIF Regulations and FPI Regulations do not mandate public disclosure of entity-wise investments. However, disclosures of investments by every AIF/FPI are in fact made to SEBI/custodians which enable regulation, detailed investigation when circumstances warrant and support policy formulation,” states SEBI. Moitra’s petition, filed as a public interest litigation (PIL), said that at a time when retail investors in mutual funds (MF) are put to strict scrutiny by SEBI, the retail investors are kept in the dark about beneficiary owners of these two funds. “Lack of public disclosure poses severe risk to financial stability, market integrity, and economic sovereignty…Increasing foreign investment into Indian market and absence of ultimate beneficiary owners disclosure norms raise concern over possible money laundering (round tripping of funds), tax evasion and market manipulation,” Moitra stated in her petition. Given the increasing role of AFIs and FPIs in the Indian financial market, the petition underlined that “regulatory transparency is crucial for protecting the interest of market stakeholders, especially retail investors.” This, in turn, would ensure market stability and prevent financial malpractices by circumventing laws,” she added. As per the petition, SEBI has 1,647 registered AIFs holding assets worth ₹ 14.17 lakh crore and 11,999 FPIs with assets worth ₹ 78.66 lakh crore.

news.headline: Supreme Court Grants Bail to Two Convicts in Bilkis Bano Case Citing Long Incarceration
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India has granted bail to two convicts, Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya, in the 2002 Bilkis Bano gang rape and murder case. A division bench comprising Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale cited their continuous imprisonment of over 17 years and pending legal points in their appeals as grounds for relief. The order comes over two years after the top court quashed the premature release of eleven life sentence convicts in the matter.
news.full_article_text:
### Judicial Decision and Directives
On October 28, a Supreme Court bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale granted bail to two convicts in the 2002 Bilkis Bano gang rape and murder case: Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya. The court noted that both individuals had undergone incarceration for more than 17 years and that their pending appeals involve substantial questions of fact and law that require adjudication. The bench also highlighted that Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi suffers from a severe physical handicap, while another key aspect noted was that one of the appellants was not named in the initial First Information Report (FIR) and was implicated only after a period of nearly three years. Bail was granted subject to terms and conditions to be determined by the trial court.

### Arguments Presented in Court
Senior advocates Sidharth Luthra and Sonia Mathur, representing Joshi and Modhiya, submitted that the appellants had served over 17 years of life imprisonment following their conviction under various sections of the Indian Penal Code related to murder and gang rape. Conversely, Additional Solicitor General Rajkumar Bhaskar Thakare, appearing on behalf of the state/prosecution, opposed the bail plea. He emphasized the gravity of the offences involving gang rape and highlighted that lower courts had carefully considered the severity of the crime and material on record when deciding prior pleas.

### Background and Chronology of Events
The case traces back to the aftermath of the burning of the Sabarmati Express at Godhra in February 2002, which triggered widespread communal riots in Gujarat. During the violence, 21-year-old Bilkis Bano, who was three months pregnant, was gang-raped, and seven of her family members, including her three-year-old daughter, were killed. In December 2003, the Supreme Court directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to investigate the case, and in August 2004, the trial was transferred out of Gujarat to Mumbai to ensure a fair trial. In 2008, a special trial court in Mumbai convicted 11 men, sentencing them to life imprisonment, an order upheld by the Bombay High Court in 2017.

### Previous Decisions on Premature Remission
In August 2022, the Gujarat state government ordered the premature release of all 11 convicts under its remission policy. However, in January 2024, the Supreme Court quashed the Gujarat government's remission order. The top court ruled that Gujarat lacked statutory authority to grant remission because the trial had been conducted in Mumbai, making the Maharashtra government the appropriate authority. Additionally, the court observed that a 2022 Supreme Court order directing Gujarat to consider remission had been obtained by suppressing material facts and practicing fraud upon the court. Following the January 2024 judgment, all convicts were directed to surrender and return to prison.
news.background_context: The case relates to the 2002 communal riots in Gujarat following the Godhra train burning incident. Bilkis Bano was gang-raped and seven family members were murdered. In 2008, 11 men were convicted by a Mumbai court. In August 2022, Gujarat granted them remission, which was struck down by the Supreme Court in January 2024 on jurisdictional grounds, directing the convicts to return to prison.

While the severity of heinous crimes like gang rape remains a paramount consideration in sentencing, prolonged incarceration pending final appeal considerations—especially exceeding 17 years—presents constitutional grounds for evaluating bail. The case also underlines key principles of criminal procedure: the jurisdiction of the 'appropriate government' in executive remission decisions depends on the place of trial rather than the place of offence.

The recent October bail order demonstrates that even in serious offences, long incarceration (over 17 years) combined with pending appeals and personal vulnerabilities (handicap, delay in FIR naming) can warrant bail under Article 21 rights.

hindi_translation.story_lead: उच्चतम न्यायालय ने 2002 के बिलकिस बानो सामूहिक बलात्कार और हत्या मामले में दो दोषियों, विपिनचंद कन्हैयालाल जोशी और प्रदीप रमणलाल मोढिया को जमानत दे दी है। न्यायमूर्ति एमएम सुंदरेश और न्यायमूर्ति पीबी वराले की पीठ ने राहत के मुख्य आधार के रूप में 17 वर्षों से अधिक की लंबी कैद और उनकी याचिकाओं में लंबित कानूनी मुद्दों का उल्लेख किया। यह आदेश शीर्ष अदालत द्वारा इस मामले में आजीवन कारावास की सजा काट रहे 11 पुरुषों की समय से पहले रिहाई को रद्द करने के दो साल बाद आया है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### न्यायिक निर्णय और निर्देश
28 अक्टूबर को न्यायमूर्ति एमएम सुंदरेश और न्यायमूर्ति पीबी वराले की सुप्रीम कोर्ट की पीठ ने 2002 के बिलकिस बानो सामूहिक बलात्कार और हत्या मामले में दो दोषियों - विपिनचंद कन्हैयालाल जोशी और प्रदीप रमणलाल मोढिया को जमानत दे दी। अदालत ने नोट किया कि दोनों व्यक्ति 17 वर्षों से अधिक समय से जेल में बंद हैं और उनकी लंबित अपीलों में तथ्य और कानून के महत्वपूर्ण प्रश्न शामिल हैं जिन पर विचार किया जाना आवश्यक है। पीठ ने यह भी रेखांकित किया कि विपिनचंद कन्हैयालाल जोशी गंभीर रूप से शारीरिक रूप से विकलांग हैं, जबकि एक अन्य पहलू यह था कि एक अपीलकर्ता का नाम प्रारंभिक प्राथमिकी (FIR) में शामिल नहीं था और घटना के लगभग तीन साल बाद उसे नामजद किया गया था। जमानत ट्रायल कोर्ट द्वारा निर्धारित शर्तों के अधीन दी गई है।

### अदालत में प्रस्तुत तर्क
जोशी और मोढिया का प्रतिनिधित्व कर रहे वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता सिद्धार्थ लूथरा और सोनिया माथुर ने तर्क दिया कि अपीलकर्ताओं ने हत्या और सामूहिक बलात्कार से संबंधित धाराओं के तहत आजीवन कारावास की सजा के दौरान 17 वर्ष से अधिक की सजा काट ली है। इसके विपरीत, राज्य/अभियोजन पक्ष की ओर से पेश हुए अतिरिक्त सॉलिसिटर जनरल राजकुमार भास्कर ठाकरे ने जमानत याचिका का विरोध किया। उन्होंने सामूहिक बलात्कार से जुड़े अपराधों की गंभीरता पर जोर दिया और कहा कि निचली अदालतों ने अपराध की गंभीरता और रिकॉर्ड पर मौजूद सामग्री पर ध्यान दिया था।

### पृष्ठभूमि और घटनाक्रम
यह मामला फरवरी 2002 में गोधरा में साबरमती एक्सप्रेस को जलाए जाने के बाद गुजरात में भड़के सांप्रदायिक दंगों से जुड़ा है। हिंसा के दौरान, 21 वर्षीय बिलकिस बानो, जो तीन महीने की गर्भवती थीं, के साथ सामूहिक बलात्कार किया गया था और उनकी तीन साल की बेटी सहित उनके परिवार के सात सदस्यों की हत्या कर दी गई थी। दिसंबर 2003 में, सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने सीबीआई को मामले की जांच का निर्देश दिया और अगस्त 2004 में निष्पक्ष सुनवाई सुनिश्चित करने के लिए मुकदमे को गुजरात से मुंबई स्थानांतरित कर दिया गया। 2008 में, मुंबई की एक विशेष अदालत ने 11 पुरुषों को दोषी ठहराते हुए आजीवन कारावास की सजा सुनाई, जिसे 2017 में बॉम्बे हाई कोर्ट ने बरकरार रखा।

### समय पूर्व रिहाई पर पिछले फैसले
अगस्त 2022 में, गुजरात सरकार ने अपनी सजा माफी नीति के तहत सभी 11 दोषियों की समय से पहले रिहाई का आदेश दिया। हालांकि, जनवरी 2024 में, सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने गुजरात सरकार के रिहाई के आदेश को रद्द कर दिया। शीर्ष अदालत ने फैसला सुनाया कि गुजरात के पास रिहाई का आदेश देने का वैधानिक अधिकार नहीं था क्योंकि मुकदमा मुंबई में चलाया गया था, जिससे महाराष्ट्र सरकार उपयुक्त प्राधिकारी बन गई थी। इसके अतिरिक्त, अदालत ने पाया कि गुजरात को रिहाई पर विचार करने का निर्देश देने वाला 2022 का आदेश तथ्यों को छिपाकर प्राप्त किया गया था। जनवरी 2024 के फैसले के बाद, सभी दोषियों को आत्मसमर्पण कर वापस जेल जाने का निर्देश दिया गया था।
hindi_translation.background_context: यह मामला गोधरा ट्रेन अग्निकांड के बाद 2002 के गुजरात दंगों से संबंधित है। बिलकिस बानो के साथ सामूहिक बलात्कार किया गया था और परिवार के 7 सदस्यों की हत्या कर दी गई थी। 2008 में मुंबई अदालत ने 11 लोगों को दोषी ठहराया था। अगस्त 2022 में गुजरात ने उन्हें समय पूर्व रिहाई दी, जिसे सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने जनवरी 2024 में अधिकार क्षेत्र के आधार पर रद्द कर दिया था।
bullet_points: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने बिलकिस बानो मामले में दो दोषियों विपिनचंद कन्हैयालाल जोशी और प्रदीप रमणलाल मोढिया को जमानत दी।
जमानत 28 अक्टूबर को न्यायमूर्ति एमएम सुंदरेश और न्यायमूर्ति पीबी वराले की पीठ द्वारा दी गई।
पीठ ने कहा कि दोनों दोषी 17 साल से अधिक समय जेल में बिता चुके हैं।
अदालत ने जोशी की शारीरिक विकलांगता और घटना के 3 साल बाद प्राथमिकी में नाम शामिल किए जाने जैसे तथ्यों को ध्यान में रखा।

जनवरी 2024 में, सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने गुजरात सरकार के अगस्त 2022 के उस आदेश को रद्द कर दिया था जिसमें 11 दोषियों को रिहा किया गया था।

quiz.question: In the Bilkis Bano case, why did the Supreme Court set aside the Gujarat government's remission order in January 2024?
options: A) The period of 14 years had not been completed by the convicts.
B) Gujarat lacked statutory jurisdiction because the trial had been conducted in Maharashtra.
C) The Central Bureau of Investigation had not given its mandatory approval.
D) The offence occurred in a Union Territory outside Gujarat's jurisdiction.
quiz.correct_answer: B) Gujarat lacked statutory jurisdiction because the trial had been conducted in Maharashtra.
quiz.explanation: In January 2024, the Supreme Court ruled that the state of Maharashtra, where the trial actually took place, was the 'appropriate government' to consider sentence remission under Section 432 of the CrPC, making Gujarat's August 2022 remission order invalid due to lack of jurisdiction.

news.headline: Elon Musk is a 'real genius', Putin says after satellite talks with SpaceX boss
news.story_lead: Russian President Vladimir Putin has promoted the country's own satellite internet project. - Published 28 October 2026 Elon Musk is a "real genius", Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday after revealing the two are in "close" contact about satellite technology. The remarks came during the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, during which Putin discussed Russia's own satellite internet project Rassvet, which provides internet connections to people from satellites.
news.full_article_text: Russian President Vladimir Putin has promoted the country's own satellite internet project. - Published 28 October 2026 Elon Musk is a "real genius", Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday after revealing the two are in "close" contact about satellite technology. The remarks came during the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, during which Putin discussed Russia's own satellite internet project Rassvet, which provides internet connections to people from satellites. "He's a genius, a real genius," Putin said of Musk, according to a translation of his remarks by the BBC. "We are in close contact with our American partners, including Mr. Musk." Starlink is part of Musk's company SpaceX. The company did not respond to a request for comment. Putin added that it was important for Russia to be in contact with Musk so Rassvet and Starlink satellites do not "interfere with each other in orbit". "We and our American partners value this mutually, and despite all the political questions, we are working hard," he said. Starlink has launched roughly 13,000 of its satellites, according to the company. By contrast there are only a couple of dozen Rassvet satellites currently in orbit, according to online satellite trackers. The Russian Embassy in South Africa said on Wednesday Rassvet is "Russia's Starlink alternative" and "marks only the country's first steps in this field". "Russia maintains close contacts with the US on space, including with Elon Musk," the embassy wrote. Putin's comments about Rassvet and Starlink were made as the US and Russia appear to be growing closer, even as it approaches five years since Putin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Ukraine relied on Starlink internet in its efforts to keep Russia's forces at bay. But its military last week suddenly suffered Starlink connectivity problems, something Musk has admitted SpaceX did intentionally. US President Donald Trump earlier this month said he'd struck a deal with Russia to import diesel in an effort to lower gas prices that have skyrocketed due to the US war with Iran. Then Trump waived certain sanctions against Russia that were set to take effect. Not long after, a US citizen was released from Russian custody, with US envoy Steve Witkoff referring to Putin as a "humanitarian". Musk was born in South Africa and then immigrated to Canada before settling in the US. All of his business ventures, including Tesla, SpaceX and Starlink, are based in America, with most operating out of California and Texas. The billionaire, and off and on again trillionaire, has been one of the biggest political allies and financiers of Trump and other Republican US politicians. Related topics

news.exam_corner_topic: Banking Regulatory Accountability & Cyber Fraud Safeguards
static_gk: Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C): Established under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to serve as a framework for law enforcement agencies to deal with cybercrimes in a coordinated manner.
Reserve Bank of India (RBI): India's central bank established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, responsible for regulating the banking system and issuing KYC guidelines.
news.headline: Supreme Court Rules Banks Must Compensate Digital Arrest Victims in Case of Due Diligence Failure
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India has held that banks and financial institutions must compensate victims of digital arrest scams if losses occur due to a failure in operational due diligence. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant urged the implementation of automated, preventive banking interventions to freeze suspicious transactions before funds leave accounts.
news.full_article_text:
### Supreme Court Directive on Banking Accountability

A Supreme Court bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, and Justice V. Mohana ruled that financial institutions must compensate fraud victims if losses stem from deficient due diligence. The apex court expressed concern over the persistence of digital arrest scams despite widespread media coverage, emphasizing that preventive measures must replace post-incident reporting.

### Examination of Proposed RBI Guidelines

* **KYC Framework Revision:** The Supreme Court is examining the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) proposed Know Your Customer (KYC) Amendment Directions, 2026, scheduled for notification by November 30 and operationalisation by December 31.
* **Banking Interventions:** The court called for automated suspension of transactions that significantly deviate from a customer's established spending patterns, real-time alerts to nearby police stations, and physical verification procedures prior to executing large or abnormal transfers.
* **Institutional Scope:** The apex court directed the RBI to submit a comprehensive list of all authorized financial institutions to enable uniform judicial directions without needing to implead individual banks.

### Extent of Cyber Fraud Losses & Incidents

According to a status report filed by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), over 21,900 digital arrest complaints were recorded between January 1 and August 31, 2026, amounting to financial losses exceeding ₹647 crore. Attorney General R. Venkataramani noted that reported cases fell by roughly 50% year-on-year, but the CJI highlighted that overall financial losses from such cyber frauds still reached nearly ₹800 crore in the current year.

### Regional Incident Reports Cited

* **Delhi:** Two individuals were apprehended for running a mule account in Yamuna Vihar linked to a ₹2.10-crore scam targeting a Janakpuri resident.
* **Hyderabad:** Cybercrime police arrested two individuals for defrauding a retired employee and his daughter of ₹29.17 lakh using mule accounts, cash deposit machines, and cryptocurrency conversions.
* **Kozhikode:** A victim lost ₹1.35 crore after extortionists impersonating Mumbai Crime Branch officials coerced her into transferring funds for fake RBI verification between September 22 and October 15.
* **Dakshina Kannada:** A farmer from Puttur taluk lost ₹1.31 crore after being kept under continuous digital arrest from September 2 to October 6, 2026, under false accusations linked to terror financing.
news.background_context: Digital arrest scams involve cybercriminals impersonating law enforcement, tax, or judicial officials over video and voice calls to intimidate victims into transferring money under the threat of immediate arrest.

hindi_translation.headline: सुप्रीम कोर्ट का आदेश: ड्यू डिलिजेंस में विफलता होने पर बैंक डिजिटल अरेस्ट पीड़ितों को मुआवजा दें
hindi_translation.story_lead: उच्चतम न्यायालय ने आदेश दिया है कि यदि उचित जांच (ड्यू डिलिजेंस) में लापरवाही के कारण धोखाधड़ी होती है, तो बैंकों और वित्तीय संस्थानों को डिजिटल अरेस्ट पीड़ितों को मुआवजा देना होगा। मुख्य न्यायाधीश सूर्या कांत की अध्यक्षता वाली पीठ ने पैसे ट्रांसफर होने से पहले संदिग्ध लेनदेन को रोकने के लिए स्वचालित उपायों का आह्वान किया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### बैंकिंग जवाबदेही पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट का निर्देश

मुख्य न्यायाधीश सूर्या कांत, न्यायमूर्ति जॉयमाल्या बागची और न्यायमूर्ति वी. मोहना की पीठ ने फैसला सुनाया कि यदि वित्तीय संस्थान अपनी उचित जांच दायित्वों को पूरा करने में विफल रहते हैं, तो उन्हें साइबर धोखाधड़ी के पीड़ितों को उचित मुआवजा देना होगा। अदालत ने जन जागरूकता अभियानों के बावजूद लोगों के डिजिटल अरेस्ट धोखाधड़ी का शिकार होने पर चिंता व्यक्त की।

### प्रस्तावित आरबीआई दिशानिर्देशों की समीक्षा

* **केवाईसी ढांचे में संशोधन:** सुप्रीम कोर्ट भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (आरबीआई) के प्रस्तावित 'नो योर कस्टमर (केवाईसी) संशोधन निर्देश, 2026' की समीक्षा करेगा, जिन्हें 30 नवंबर तक अधिसूचित और 31 दिसंबर तक लागू किया जाना है।
* **बैंक स्तर पर निवारक उपाय:** अदालत ने खाते के सामान्य पैटर्न से अलग असामान्य लेनदेन को तुरंत रोकने, संदिग्ध गतिविधियों की स्वचालित रिपोर्टिंग और बड़े हस्तांतरण से पहले भौतिक सत्यापन की मांग की।
* **व्यापक दायरा:** पीठ ने आरबीआई को सभी अधिकृत वित्तीय संस्थानों की सूची सौंपने का निर्देश दिया ताकि व्यक्तिगत बैंकों को पक्षकार बनाए बिना सर्वव्यापी निर्देश जारी किए जा सकें।

### साइबर धोखाधड़ी के आंकड़े और मामले

गृह मंत्रालय (MHA) और भारतीय साइबर अपराध समन्वय केंद्र (I4C) की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, 1 जनवरी से 31 अगस्त 2026 के बीच डिजिटल अरेस्ट धोखाधड़ी की 21,900 से अधिक शिकायतें दर्ज की गईं, जिनमें ₹647 करोड़ से अधिक की हानि हुई। अटॉर्नी जनरल आर. वेंकटरमणी ने बताया कि दर्ज मामलों में पिछले वर्ष की तुलना में लगभग 50% की कमी आई है, लेकिन सीजेआई ने रेखांकित किया कि इस वर्ष इस प्रकार के अपराधों से कुल नुकसान लगभग ₹800 करोड़ तक पहुंच गया है।

### देशभर से सामने आए प्रमुख मामले

* **दिल्ली:** जनकपुरी के एक निवासी से ₹2.10 करोड़ की ठगी के मामले में यमुना विहार में एक म्यूल खाता चलाने वाले दो लोगों को गिरफ्तार किया गया।
* **हैदराबाद:** साइबर क्राइम पुलिस ने एक सेवानिवृत्त कर्मचारी और उनकी बेटी से ₹29.17 लाख ठगने के आरोप में दो लोगों को गिरफ्तार किया।
* **कोझिकोड:** मुंबई क्राइम ब्रांच के अधिकारी बनकर जालसाजों ने एक महिला से फर्जी आरबीआई सत्यापन के नाम पर ₹1.35 करोड़ ऐंठ लिए।
* **दक्षिण कन्नड़:** पुत्तूर तालुक के एक किसान को 2 सितंबर से 6 अक्टूबर 2026 तक डिजिटल अरेस्ट में रखकर ₹1.31 करोड़ की ठगी की गई।

news.exam_corner_topic: ‘Orders becoming a mockery’: Supreme Court pulls up Delhi govt over firecracker curbs
news.headline: ‘Orders becoming a mockery’: Supreme Court pulls up Delhi govt over firecracker curbs
news.story_lead: ‘Orders becoming a mockery’: Supreme Court pulls up Delhi govt over firecracker curbs A bench questioned the authorities over the lack of concrete data on enforcement and the impact of measures taken to curb pollution in Delhi-NCR. The Supreme Court on Thursday pulled up the Delhi government and the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) for not adequately enforcing curbs on the sale and use of firecrackers, but reiterated its position that a complete ban was not the solution to the problem of pollution during the festive season. The top court indicated that it was likely to allow the sale and bursting of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR for a limited period on specified days this Diwali, though it reserved its order on a fresh interim arrangement.
news.full_article_text: ‘Orders becoming a mockery’: Supreme Court pulls up Delhi govt over firecracker curbs A bench questioned the authorities over the lack of concrete data on enforcement and the impact of measures taken to curb pollution in Delhi-NCR. The Supreme Court on Thursday pulled up the Delhi government and the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) for not adequately enforcing curbs on the sale and use of firecrackers, but reiterated its position that a complete ban was not the solution to the problem of pollution during the festive season. The top court indicated that it was likely to allow the sale and bursting of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR for a limited period on specified days this Diwali, though it reserved its order on a fresh interim arrangement. It noted that the three-day relaxation granted for the festival in October 2025 was a one-time measure that could not automatically be extended. Diwali falls on November 8 this year. A bench of justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale spoke about the public sentiment attached to Diwali celebrations but stressed that authorities could not use festive enthusiasm as an excuse for failing to enforce firecracker restrictions. “We also understand the sentiment of the public. Somebody wants to celebrate. Therefore, we are not inclined to impose a complete ban because, again, it will have a spiralling effect. But then, having said that, please don’t push us to take a very harsh stand on this matter,” the bench observed, pointing out that the authorities must demonstrate tangible action rather than merely promise better enforcement. Deep Dive The court said that it was not asking the authorities to prevent people from celebrating Diwali but to ensure that firecrackers were used responsibly and only within the permitted window. It suggested that officials should concentrate their enforcement efforts on the designated days, even if that meant forgoing their own festival celebrations to monitor compliance, issue challans, cancel licences, and prosecute violators. “During festivals, enthusiasm among the public is high. They are normal people. We cannot file cases against them, but what you can do is ensure our orders are implemented…Change of mind of public will take time. We have different people…children, women etc. We have to take care of everybody…Every year we pass orders. It becomes very academic,” it said. ALSO READ | ‘Delhi's air will be very bad after Diwali’: SC judge on request to defer a hearing The hearing brought into focus a recurring problem in the Capital’s battle against winter pollution: the gap between restrictions imposed by the courts and their enforcement in the marketplace and on the ground. The bench sought details of inspections, seizures and other action taken under previous orders, making it clear that claims of preparedness would carry little weight without evidence of their impact. “After our order last year, what did you actually do? See now, otherwise, there is no point in passing orders and issuing all these conditions, unless on the ground you really give effect to it. It becomes near mockery then,” the bench remarked. The court’s reluctance to impose a blanket prohibition follows its September 30 decision to permit specified next-generation green firecracker chains, or laris, subject to prescribed safeguards, while keeping the question of barium-containing crackers open for further scientific assessment. The bench said at the time that a total ban would hurt public sentiments, while unrestricted bursting throughout the day would seriously affect children, the elderly and the sick. To be sure, questions remain on whether the permitted products are genuinely less polluting. There is no evidence from previous years that using green firecrackers in place of conventional ones has blunted the spike in pollution during Diwali. The proceedings arise from a 2015 petition filed on behalf of three minors seeking a blanket ban on the sale and use of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, citing the harmful effects of air pollution on children and other vulnerable groups. The Supreme Court subsequently imposed several restrictions, including a ban on barium salts in fireworks and on joined firecrackers, before permitting limited use of specified green crackers under regulated conditions. In 2025, the court partially modified its ban-on-firecrackers order of April 3, 2025 in Delhi-NCR by permitting the sale and bursting of crackers between October 18 and 20, coinciding with Diwali, under specified timings. That Diwali, Delhi recorded its worst festival pollution peak since 2021. HT’s analysis of eight monitoring stations with consistent data found that average PM2.5 concentrations peaked at 785.6 micrograms per cubic metre on Diwali night, the equivalent of an AQI of 812 on an index officially capped at 500. Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Union government, told the bench that an enforcement mechanism was in place for this year but had not been presented to the court. The court, however, insisted that the authorities demonstrate what had actually been done to prevent the sale and use of prohibited firecrackers and to ensure compliance with the restrictions. ALSO READ | Gurugram police form several teams to crack down on illegal firecracker sale ahead of Diwali The amici curiae, senior advocates Aparajita Singh and Uttara Babbar, and lawyers representing the petitioners, including senior counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan, questioned the effectiveness of the previous year’s relaxation, pointing to the use of banned crackers, gaps in monitoring, and the lack of comprehensive data on enforcement. The bench also sought information on the functioning of CAQM’s monitoring network, noting concerns over the number of operational monitoring units and the absence of reliable records of field inspections. The court’s latest deliberations suggest that the immediate question goes beyond which categories of firecrackers should be allowed, to whether the authorities can ensure that only permitted products are sold and used during the limited hours authorised by the court. ALSO READ | Lawyers can work from home, we can’t: Supreme Court judge on post-Diwali air in Delhi The bench on Thursday also proposed a public awareness campaign involving prominent personalities and sportspersons, suggesting that cricketer Virat Kohli or other respected public figures could encourage people to celebrate a less-polluting Diwali. It sought to distinguish the festival’s religious and cultural significance from the practice of bursting firecrackers, observing that the celebration of light need not depend on fireworks. “Otherwise, you know, we light the lamp and then everybody will do it in a necessary way and then, you know, it is so beautiful; just at the end of the day it is fire,” observed the bench, adding that religious faith and the practices associated with it were distinct. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Utkarsh Anand Utkarsh Anand is the

It noted that the three-day relaxation granted for the festival in October 2025 was a one-time measure that could not automatically be extended. Diwali falls on November 8 this year.

A bench of justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale spoke about the public sentiment attached to Diwali celebrations but stressed that authorities could not use festive enthusiasm as an excuse for failing to enforce firecracker restrictions.

“We also understand the sentiment of the public. Somebody wants to celebrate. Therefore, we are not inclined to impose a complete ban because, again, it will have a spiralling effect. But then, having said that, please don’t push us to take a very harsh stand on this matter,” the bench observed, pointing out that the authorities must demonstrate tangible action rather than merely promise better enforcement.

* **Core Directive:** The apex court highlighted the severity of financial losses suffered by account holders targeted by fraudsters impersonating law enforcement personnel.
* **Regulatory Responsibility:** The RBI, as India's central banking regulator, was requested to formulate rules requiring financial institutions to address victim liabilities and compensate affected consumers.
* **Objective:** The move aims to enforce stricter cyber-security compliance among commercial banks and safeguard public confidence in digital banking channels.

news.headline: Bar Bodies Foiled Plan to Engage Former Judges, Observes Supreme Court
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India observed that efforts to engage former judges to tackle court backlog were foiled due to opposition from bar associations. The remark underlines institutional challenges in executing ad-hoc appointments aimed at reducing case pendency.
news.full_article_text:
### Supreme Court Observation on Engagement of Retired Judges

The Supreme Court of India stated that proposals to rope in former judges to help clear case pendency were thwarted due to resistance from legal bar bodies.

- **Core Issue:** The apex court noted that plans aimed at utilizing the services of retired judges were stalled by bar associations.
- **Judicial Pendency:** Mechanisms to re-engage experienced former judges have been considered as an ad-hoc measure to accelerate case disposal and reduce judicial backlog across the court system.
- **Friction with Bar Associations:** Resistance from legal bar bodies reflects ongoing differences between the bench and bar regarding ad-hoc appointments and temporary judicial engagements.

The proposal was intended to address rising case pendency and assist in clearing backlogs.
Resistance from bar associations prevented the execution of the initiative.
Ad-hoc judge engagement is seen as a short-term mechanism to boost judicial capacity.
The observation highlights institutional coordination challenges in implementing court reforms.

The initiative targeted case pendency reduction through temporary judge appointments.

news.upsc_analysis: The Supreme Court's observation brings out the broader policy dilemma in judicial administration: while ad-hoc appointments of retired judges offer a quick mechanism to tackle massive backlogs, structural friction with legal bar associations can impede implementation.
